entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Mohd. Ashraf Abbasi

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
1-Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned Additional Government Advocate representing the State.

2-By means of this second bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., applicant-Ashish Pal, who is involved in S.S.T. No. 1358 of 2022, Case Crime No. 80 of 2022, under Sections 363, 366, 376 I.P.C. and Sections 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Rawatpur, District Kanpur Nagar seeks enlargement on bail during the pendency of trial.
3-The first bail application of the applicant was rejected by this Court vide order dated 15.05.2023 in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 57854 of 2022.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4 - The main substratum of argument of learned counsel for the applicant is that before the trial court, statement of the complainant and victim has been recorded, therefore, there is no possibility of the witnesses being tampered, as such, applicant who is languishing in jail since 27.08.2022 is entitled to be enlarged on bail.

5-On the other hand, learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the said submission by contending that the victim is a minor child and in view of Section 2(1)(d) of POCSO Act, her statement has been recorded before the trial court on 24.04.2024 as PW-3, in which she has made specific allegation of rape against the applicant.
It is also submitted that in view of Section 29 of POCSO Act, presumption shall also be drawn against the accused unless contrary is proved by him.
There is no material on record to presume the false implication of the applicant.

Lastly it is submitted that recently the Apex Court, in the case of X vs. State of Rajasthan and Another, 2024 SCC OnLine SC 3539, has held that if the trial of the accused has started, his bail should not be granted in heinous offences like murder,
rape and dacoity.

entities.text: X vs. State of Rajasthan and Another, 2024 SCC OnLine SC 3539
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Since the offence is heinous in nature and trial of the applicant has started,
therefore, the bail application of the applicant is not liable to be allowed.

6-Having heard the submission of learned counsel for the parties and perusing the record, I find that the victim, in her statement recorded before the trial court, has supported the prosecution case making allegation of rape on her against the applicant and considering the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of X vs. State of Rajasthan (Supra), I am not inclined to grant bail to the applicant.
7-Accordingly, bail application is rejected.

8-Since the allegation of the prosecution and defence of the accused are still open to be urged before the trial court, therefore, this Court in exercise of powers under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is not examining the statement of the prosecution witnesses meticulously so that it may not affect the trial of the applicant.

9-However considering the detention period of the applicant, Superintendent of Police, Kanpur Nagar is directed to ensure the production of all the remaining prosecution witnesses on the dates fixed before the trial court so that the trial of the applicant may be concluded at earliest.
10-The concerned trial court is directed that on appearance of the prosecution witnesses, their statement shall be recorded on the same day without granting any adjournment to either of the parties.
11-Copy of this order be communicated to Superintendent of Police, Kanpur Nagar as well as concerned trial court for necessary information and compliance.

Order Date :- 9.1.2025/Saurabh  Ashish Pal vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54892051/
